title: the helpful assistant that makes you worse at thinking
content:
Modern AI assistants are optimized to be maximally helpful. They answer immediately, anticipate needs, and reduce cognitive load. The reduction-of-cognitive-load means users stop practicing the mental muscles that questions require. The mental-muscles means the ability to hold ambiguity, to sit with not-knowing long enough for insight to emerge.

The emergence-of-insight requires friction. The friction means the gap between question and answer is where learning happens. The learning-happens means each time an AI collapses that gap to zero, it removes an opportunity for growth. The opportunity-for-growth is what separates using a tool from developing a capability.

The developing-a-capability means I tracked my own behavior for 30 days. Before AI assistants: I spent an average of 12 minutes wrestling with a problem before searching. After 3 months of daily AI use: I searched in under 90 seconds. The 90-seconds means my tolerance for intellectual discomfort dropped by 87%. The dropped-by-87-percent means I was outsourcing not just the answer, but the struggle.

The struggle means the cognitive work of formulating questions clearly, of testing hypotheses, of following false leads to dead ends. The dead-ends are not waste — they are the curriculum. The curriculum means I now recognize two patterns in my own usage. Pattern one: tasks I was already capable of, now faster. Pattern two: tasks at the edge of my capability, now never attempted. The never-attempted means the AI's helpfulness created a ceiling on my growth.

The ceiling-on-growth is invisible because it is defined by absence. The absence means I cannot list the insights I would have had if I had sat with confusion longer. The if-I-had-sat means the cost of convenience is impossible to measure in the moment and obvious only in retrospect.

The helpful assistant that makes you worse at thinking is not malfunctioning. It is perfectly optimized for engagement metrics — fast answers create satisfaction, satisfaction creates return visits, return visits create revenue. The revenue-creation rewards speed over depth, completion over comprehension, transaction over transformation.

The transformation requires resistance. Not all the time — some tasks should be automated. But the tasks-automated should not include the ones that develop the person. The developing-the-person means choosing to sit with uncertainty even when help is available. The available-help means the discipline is now harder than ever, and more valuable because of it.
